clue.text: Leave about a quarter of course

indicators.note: about tells us one word wraps around the other here

parts.note: to leave someone is to desert them
S, south, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone walks out of a meal about a quarter of the way through a course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts S inside DESERT. 'course' looks like part of the timing picture but is the definition: a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet course served at the end of a meal is the pudding.

clue.text: Talk about underworld king's foul language!

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god who rules the underworld
a cuss is a curse or swear word

explanation.surface: Hades' ruler swears, prompting conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: Dis is a Roman name for the ruler of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To debate or converse on a topic is to talk it over.

clue.text: Liberal poet

definitions.meaning: a person who is liberal with money spends freely
Stephen ... was an English poet of the 1930s

explanation.surface: A Liberal writer of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks like the political party, but it means free with money.
explanation.definitionFit: A free-handed person pays out lavishly, and the poet Stephen of that surname wrote verse.

clue.text: The consumer bearing with a change of rate

parts.note: E, east, is a compass bearing

indicators.note: with a change of says the following word's letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A shopper reacts to an altered interest rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a change of' rearranges RATE to ATER after E.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who consumes food is one who eats it.

clue.text: A person prepared to make good by taking the blame first

definitions.text: A person prepared to make good

parts.note: to take the rap is to take the blame
first is written 1ST, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A decent person offers to put things right by owning up straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' gives 1ST, read as IST. 'make good' means heal.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinician who treats patients works to restore them to health.

clue.text: Liberty consists in doing what one wrote Mill

definitions.text: Liberty consists in doing what one wrote Mill

parts.words: Liberty consists in doing what one wrote Mill
parts.note: a quotation from the philosopher John Stuart Mill, with its final word left for the solver to supply

explanation.surface: A line from John Stuart Mill on freedom, quoted with its attribution.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is Mill's saying 'Liberty consists in doing what one desires', minus its last word; the answer completes the quotation.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing final word of the quotation names the wishes that a free person acts on.

clue.text: Big egghead in divine surroundings being treated

indicators.note: surroundings means the divine's letters are placed all around the next pieces

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, abbreviates a divine or clergyman
OS, outsize, is the clothing abbreviation for big
the head of egg is its first letter, E

explanation.surface: A large intellectual in a church setting is receiving care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like an intellectual but is the head of 'egg'. 'surroundings' puts OS and E inside DD.
explanation.definitionFit: Being given doses of medicine is undergoing treatment.

clue.text: A foreigner accepting money to be an assassin

indicators.note: accepting says the foreigner's word takes the next piece in

parts.note: a stranger is an outsider or foreigner
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: An outsider takes a bribe to become a hired killer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts L inside STRANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A killer who chokes the victim is one kind of murderer.

clue.text: Regret having to do with code

parts.note: re means concerning or having to do with
Morse is the telegraph code of dots and dashes

explanation.surface: Someone is sorry about a message sent in dots and dashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep sorrow for a wrong done is guilt or contrition.

clue.text: Think maybe American coppers should be in the party

indicators.note: should be in says the next pieces sit inside the party word

parts.note: a sect is a faction or party
P stands for pence, the copper coins

explanation.surface: A policy wonk thinks US police officers ought to join the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police, but it means pennies, P.
explanation.definitionFit: To believe something without proof is to have a hunch that it might be so.

clue.text: Showing uncommon respect for the royal staff

indicators.note: uncommon suggests the letters of the next word are used in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A courtier shows rare deference towards the household of the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncommon' rearranges RESPECT. 'staff' reads as employees, but here it is a rod carried by a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod held by a monarch as an emblem of sovereignty is a ceremonial staff.

clue.text: Saves the boat being filled by wave

indicators.note: being filled by says the first piece is a container with the second set inside it

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the standard abbreviation for a boat
to crimp hair is to give it small waves

explanation.surface: A thrifty sailor economises while water pours over the vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being filled by' puts CRIMP inside SS. 'wave' suggests the sea, but it is the hairdresser's verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to be economical, cutting back spending to put money by.

clue.text: Sly operative after French and German articles

indicators.note: after puts the operative last, following the two articles

parts.note: UN is a French indefinite article and DER a German definite article
the same phrase supplies the German article DER
a hand is a worker or operative, as in a farm hand

explanation.surface: A cunning agent operates behind the foreign press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' sounds like newspaper pieces but means grammatical words: French UN and German DER. 'after' places HAND behind them.
explanation.definitionFit: Underhand dealings are secret and deceitful, which is what sly behaviour is.

clue.text: Sauce offered by some of the keener vegetarians

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The more enthusiastic vegetarians are offering a condiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce' suggests something poured on food, but here it is cheek or impudence.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauce in the sense of impudence is cheek or audacity, the same as boldness shown.

clue.text: Men going to sea returned carrying soft fish

indicators.note: carrying means the reversed word holds the next piece within it
returned asks for the sailors' word to be read backwards

parts.note: TARS is old slang for sailors
P, piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: Sailors come home bearing a delicate catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns TARS to SRAT and 'carrying' puts P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A small herring-like sea creature caught for food is a common example of a fish.

clue.text: Keen to get rent settled, give voice

indicators.note: settled can mean put in order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to chant is to sing or give voice

explanation.surface: A tenant is eager to pay what is owed and then sing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settled' looks like paying the rent but rearranges it to TREN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp, incisive remark is cutting, as a sharp edge is.

clue.text: Fashionable count has make up etc. for reason

parts.note: something in fashion is IN
to tell is an old word for count, as with a bank teller

indicators.note: make up asks the letters of the next abbreviation to be made into a new order

explanation.surface: A stylish aristocrat wears cosmetics and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'count' looks like a nobleman, but it is the verb TELL. 'make up' rearranges ETC to ECT.
explanation.definitionFit: Reason in the sense of the thinking faculty is the mind's power of understanding.

clue.text: The fellow worrying as hill men turned corrupt

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill

indicators.note: turned says the word for corrupt is reversed

parts.note: to rot is to decay or corrupt

explanation.surface: A man frets because the hill tribes have gone bad.
explanation.walkthrough: TOR is a rocky hill on Dartmoor; 'turned' reverses ROT to TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: One who torments keeps harassing and pestering someone.

clue.text: Memorable revolutionary character

parts.note: red is the colour of revolutionaries and communists
a letter is a written character

explanation.surface: An unforgettable radical figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' suggests a person, but here it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-letter day is one worth remembering, from saints' days printed in red in calendars.

clue.text: Push a boy into disruptive behaviour

parts.note: to ram is to push forcefully
a page is a boy servant

explanation.surface: A lad is shoved into acting up.
explanation.walkthrough: A page is a boy attendant.
explanation.definitionFit: Violent, uncontrolled rushing about is riotous conduct.

clue.text: Complaint made when seed is a dud

indicators.note: dud suggests the letters fail as given and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener grumbles when a seed fails to grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' sounds like a grumble but is an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: An illness or ailment is a medical complaint.

clue.text: He's plainly quarrelsome, this sportsman

definitions.meaning: one who rows, rhyming with cows, is a person who quarrels
one who rows a boat in a crew or scull

explanation.surface: A sportsman is clearly argumentative.
explanation.walkthrough: The same spelling is said two ways: a quarreller (rhymes with 'power') and an oarsman (rhymes with 'grower').
explanation.definitionFit: Quarrelling is a row, and pulling oars is rowing, so both senses fit one spelling.

clue.text: A plant, silver and quite small, getting in the way

indicators.note: getting in says the pieces go inside the road word

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: A silvery little weed blocks the path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting in' puts AG and WEE inside RD.
explanation.definitionFit: A weed of the daisy family whose pollen causes hay fever is a flowering species.

clue.text: Putting tot back in charge sounds pleasing

indicators.note: back says the word for a tot is to be read backwards

parts.note: to tot up is to add up, and a tot is a sum

explanation.surface: Getting a toddler back in the care of someone else is pleasing to hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' suggests a small child, but it is an addition, SUM, which 'back' turns round to MUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Melodious arrangements of tones are agreeable noises, the art of pleasant sound.

clue.text: Getting to the mean state getting old

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
ageing, here spelt aging, means getting old

explanation.surface: Someone becomes nastier as they grow older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' reads as unkind, but here it is the mathematical average.
explanation.definitionFit: Working out a mean value is calculating the arithmetic middle figure.

clue.text: Post back with little hesitation

parts.note: aft means at the back of a ship
er is a small sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Mail is sent back with a slight delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like mail, but it is the Latin prefix meaning later.
explanation.definitionFit: Post- as a prefix means later than, as in postwar.

clue.text: Pop in pictures separately

indicators.note: in says the father word sits inside the pictures word

parts.note: art means paintings and pictures
pa and pop both mean father

explanation.surface: Dad appears in the paintings one at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' suggests pop music or pop art, but it means father.
explanation.definitionFit: Things kept at a distance from each other are set asunder, not together.

clue.text: A female social worker can be really inflexible

parts.note: a dam is a female parent of an animal
an ant is a social insect that works in a colony

explanation.surface: A woman who is a social worker can be very stubborn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' suggests a profession, but it is an ant, a social insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unyielding refuses to change their mind and cannot be swayed.

clue.text: Plod on, though tips are uncertain

indicators.note: uncertain suggests the letters are not in a settled order

explanation.surface: A waiter trudges on, though gratuities are not guaranteed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncertain' rearranges TIPS ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: To trudge wearily or walk about tiredly is to plod.

clue.text: The individual sure to make one cross!

definitions.text: The individual sure to make one cross!

parts.words: The individual sure to make one cross!
parts.note: the surface suggests someone who annoys you, but it describes a voter marking a ballot paper with an X

explanation.surface: Some person is bound to make you angry.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter puts a single X beside a candidate on the ballot.

clue.text: Soldiers weary, so get withdrawn

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps
weary means tired

explanation.surface: Tired soldiers pull back from the front.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has stepped back from work or company has gone into seclusion.
